claims.text: Calling toString on an Output<T> in Pulumi produces placeholder text like `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` instead of the resolved value.

A documentation page titled 'Output value errors' exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ and covers this and other symptoms of treating an output as if it were already a plain value.
The placeholder text `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` can appear in a log line, a generated file, or a resource property when a Pulumi output is treated as a plain value.
A Pulumi docs troubleshooting page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ covering errors from stringifying, branching on, or reading a Pulumi output value like a plain value.
Pulumi Cloud returns the error '409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress' when an update is already in progress.
Crashes or hangs on Apple Silicon can be caused by x86_64 binaries running under Rosetta 2.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends the logs from a failed operation to the Pulumi team.
A recently deleted stack can be recovered from the Pulumi Cloud console, including after an accidental `pulumi stack rm --force`.
The Pulumi CLI supports `--target` and `--exclude` flags to limit operations to specific resources.
Reading `.pulumi/meta.yaml` errors occur when the CLI can't access a self-managed (DIY) state backend.
Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values because their real values are not known until the resource has been created or updated.

Converting a Pulumi Output to a string directly (instead of via apply or an equivalent helper) does not raise an error by default; Pulumi silently substitutes a placeholder message in place of the value.

In the Pulumi TypeScript SDK, the string conversion of an Output contains the literal text `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `apply` or `pulumi.interpolate`.
In the Pulumi TypeScript SDK, calling `JSON.stringify()` on an Output produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than the value.
In the Pulumi Python SDK, converting an Output to a string yields text containing `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported`, and Pulumi also logs a warning.
In Python, passing a Pulumi Output to `json.dumps()` fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`; `Output.json_dumps()` is the alternative.
In Pulumi Go, passing a `pulumi.StringOutput` where a `string` is expected is a compile error; values are resolved with `ApplyT`.
In the Pulumi C# SDK, the string conversion of an Output contains the literal text `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `Apply` or `Output.Format`.

Setting the environment variable `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true` (supported in TypeScript, Python, and C#) makes converting an Output to a string throw an exception instead of returning placeholder text.

The string-composition helpers are `pulumi.interpolate` and `pulumi.concat` in TypeScript, `Output.concat`/`Output.format`/`Output.json_dumps` in Python, `pulumi.Sprintf`/`pulumi.JSONMarshal` in Go, and `Output.Format` in C#.
A Pulumi `apply` callback runs asynchronously once the output resolves, generally after the program's top-level code has finished running.
Most Pulumi resource inputs accept outputs as well as plain values, but a resource's logical name cannot be an output.

In dynamically typed languages an `if` on a Pulumi Output is generally always true because the Output object is evaluated; in statically typed languages it is usually a compile error because `Output<bool>` is not `bool`.
Values known at program start, such as stack config read with `pulumi.Config`, environment variables, or hardcoded flags, are plain values that can be branched on normally.
Passing an Output as a resource logical name, loop bound, or map key fails to compile in TypeScript, Go, and C#.
In Python, passing an Output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`.
In Python, `range(some_output)` with a Pulumi Output raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Python, using a Pulumi Output as a dictionary key does not raise; it silently keys on the Output object itself.
Pulumi has no supported way to block the program and read a resolved value from an Output synchronously.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output from the CLI after a deployment.
The Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the result of running an update (e.g. `res.Outputs` in Go).

Linked docs pages exist: /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/apply/, /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/all/, /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/#outputs, /docs/iac/concepts/stacks/#stackreferences, /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/.
